chunks: And Abu Usamah narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Regarding a woman who intentionally killed a man, he عليه السلام said: “If his family wishes to kill her, they may kill her, and no one commits a crime for more than his own soul.”

key_terms.أَهْلُهُ: his family; the slain person’s kin who hold the right of retaliation
key_terms.جِنَايَةً: a crime or offense, especially in a legal context
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدَةً: intentionally; indicating deliberate action in the killing
key_terms.نَفْسِهِ: his own self; indicating personal legal responsibility
key_terms.يَجْنِي: commits an offense; incurs criminal liability

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman intentionally kills a man in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who intentionally kills a man, stating that the slain man’s family may seek retaliatory execution. It also establishes the principle of individual liability: no person bears criminal responsibility beyond their own self.
